D.t: Jermaine Johnson trails by 7.2 and wins 15% of simulations. Closing it takes about 72,904 voters switching sides, or 145,808 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +15.6 and D +1.7. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +8.1. Your best recent poll is Rasmussen Reports (R) at R +6.6; your worst is Trafalgar Group (R) at R +14.9. 11 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Richland, a projected net 67,584 votes; Charleston, a projected net 31,389 votes; Orangeburg, a projected net 11,755 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: York, R +7.2, 5.7% of the vote; Berkeley, R +4.0, 4.3% of the vote; Beaufort, R +7.1, 4.1% of the vote; Dorchester, R +0.2, 3.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jermaine Johnson runs furthest behind in Greenville, Oconee, Lancaster. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 46 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.29 points; Voters without a degree, 62% of voters, 46 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.11 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 59% of voters, 48 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.96 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Jermaine Johnson: Immigration voters 14 to 84, Incomes $125K and up 36 to 62, White voters 36 to 62. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$136K cash against $1.7M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points away from Jermaine Johnson. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Cash: $1.7M in the bank against $136K for Jermaine Johnson.

R.t: Alan Wilson leads by 7.2 in the forecast and wins 85% of simulations. The cushion is about 145,808 votes; a one point swing is about 10,196 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +1.7 and R +15.6. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +8.1. Your best recent poll is Trafalgar Group (R) at R +14.9; your worst is Rasmussen Reports (R) at R +6.6. 11 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Horry, a projected net 42,658 votes; Greenville, a projected net 37,690 votes; Spartanburg, a projected net 32,038 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: York, R +7.2, 5.7% of the vote; Berkeley, R +4.0, 4.3% of the vote; Beaufort, R +7.1, 4.1% of the vote; Dorchester, R +0.2, 3.0% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Alan Wilson runs furthest behind in Sumter, Dorchester, Georgetown. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 52 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.29 points; Voters without a degree, 62% of voters, 52 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.11 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 59% of voters, 50 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.96 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Alan Wilson: Black voters 20 to 78, Independents 28 to 68, Health care and Social Security voters 36 to 62. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.7M cash against $136K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points toward Alan Wilson. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
